subject: Hosted vs Dedicated — Latency/Throughput Follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finpay.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 24 Feb 2027 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted vs Dedicated — Post-call recap & next steps

Alex — great to speak earlier. Quick recap from our call and suggested next steps so we can align internally:

Summary of FinPay requirements
- Use case: real-time transaction scoring + policy enforcement (low latency, high availability)
- Typical payload: short prompts (avg ~40–80 tokens)
- Throughput: ~250 qps sustained, daily peaks up to ~800 qps for 15–30 minute windows
- Latency target: p95 target ~150ms (you mentioned aiming for 120–150ms)
- Data sensitivity: transaction-level PII; procurement indicated preference for dedicated or private deployment options

Decision factors we discussed
- Hosted API: fastest to get started (no infra commitments), good for functional validation; under heavy sustained qps p95 can drift higher due to multi-tenant batching behavior
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and lower latency variance; recommended when you have sustained throughput commitments and strict p95 SLOs
- Private (VPC/on-prem): for strict compliance/air-gapped needs — more setup time and licensing discussions

Our recommendation (based on your numbers):
- Short term: run a 48–72 hour Dedicated pilot (reserved pool) so we can validate p95 under your realistic traffic patterns and tune batching/KV caching/quantization profiles
- Medium term: if procurement prefers to avoid long-term commitments, consider starting with Hosted for a quick proof and migrating to Dedicated once we validate latency/cost

Proposed next steps
1) I’ll share a proposed pilot plan + test harness (48hr load test, canary rollout, success criteria: sustained 250 qps with p95 <= 150ms). (attached: redwood_solution_brief.pdf)
2) Please loop in Procurement / Security for SOC2 snapshot and PoC paperwork. We’ve attached a SOC2 snapshot for initial review.
3) Neha / Vivek will provide an estimate for committed capacity (monthly commit) and a sample configuration mapping to expected latency/throughput.

Let me know if I missed anything. If this sounds right I’ll send the pilot plan and proposed dates — earliest availability is next week.

Thanks,

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.inference

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finpay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@finpay.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Feb 2027 18:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated — Post-call recap & next steps

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. A few quick clarifications from our side:

- Latency: our internal SLA will be p95 <= 150ms for decisioning in the happy path. We can tolerate slightly higher p99 for very short spikes, but p95 is the hard requirement.
- Budget: we’re evaluating committed vs usage-based spend. Can you include an estimated monthly commit (and the approximate uplift vs Hosted pay-as-you-go) in the pilot plan? Procurement asked for a ballpark before scheduling a formal PO review.
- Compliance: please send SOC2 and a short explanation of data handling for transaction-level PII. We’ll send redlines to procurement if needed.

Also: is there an expected time to scale from 250 qps to 800 qps in the Dedicated pool during peaks? We want to understand ramp/scale latency.

If the pilot confirms p95 <= 150ms at sustained 250 qps, we’re likely to move forward with a committed capacity conversation.

Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Platform Operations | FinPay
alex.johnson@finpay.com
Attachment requested: SOC2 + data handling summary

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 25 Feb 2027 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated — Post-call recap & next steps

Alex — looping in some technical detail and an initial sizing estimate for the pilot. High-level notes below, followed by the proposed pilot configuration and expected outcomes.

Technical notes
- Workload shape: short prompts (~40–80 tokens) with small response sizes. This maps well to throughput-optimized configs with aggressive batching and KV cache hits when requests share prefixes.
- Latency drivers: per-token generation cost + network hop. On Dedicated we can tune GPU kernels and avoid noisy neighbors, which reduces tail latency variance.

Pilot sizing & expected performance
- Recommended pilot: 48-hour Dedicated pool (reserved) using 2 worker nodes (NVIDIA A100-equivalent) with autoscale buffer for short peaks.
- Estimated sustained throughput: 250 qps with p95 latency in the ~80–140ms window (varies with exact prompt length and model choice).
- Peak handling: with autoscale buffer we can absorb short 800 qps spikes but recommend a warm-up policy (30–60s ramp) to avoid cold allocations impacting p95. If FinPay needs instant-for-peaks, we should size additional burst nodes in Dedicated commit.
- Hosted API expectation: functional validation possible but p95 under sustained 250 qps typically falls in the 120–220ms range depending on batch timing and multi-tenant load.

Costs / commit guidance
- I’ll send a quick estimate for 1-month pilot commit vs Hosted pay-as-you-go in a follow-up. Rough rule: Dedicated committed pools reduce per-token cost by ~25–45% vs Hosted at sustained throughput while improving latency stability. Exact numbers depend on model/quantization.

Next steps (technical)
1) We’ll share a short test harness + synthetic traffic script to mirror your qps distribution.
2) Schedule a 30-minute tech prep call (Vivek + FinPay infra) to wire up the test endpoints and sample dataset (PII will be redacted).
3) Start pilot once procurement approves the temporary pilot order (48h).

Attaching a small latency report from a similar customer workload for reference (finpay_latency_report.pdf).

—
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.inference

Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated — Post-call recap & next steps

Thanks everyone — that all looks reasonable. Procurement is reviewing the SOC2 snapshot now. We’re comfortable moving forward with the 48-hour Dedicated pilot you proposed, pending a short PO for the pilot window. Can you send the DocuSign/PO link and the pilot plan so procurement can fast-track approval?

Also: please include an initial estimate for a monthly commit that would give us the ability to sustain 250 qps with a small burst buffer to handle the 800 qps spikes (we don’t need to size for constant 800 qps).

If procurement OKs the PO this week, we can target pilot start next Tue (2 Mar).

Alex
Attachment requested: DocuSign link + pilot plan
